strings.(글래스턴 중앙 광장을 둘러보고 있던 %s의 앞으로 따뜻한 바람이 불어온: (A warm breeze brushes past %s while you look around Glaston's central plaza. A flower petal, perhaps carried on that breeze, falls before %s.)
Where did it come from? The fragrance is wonderful...
strings.(살며시 다가오는 향에 발걸음이 이끌리듯 자연스레 움직인다. 그렇게 몇: (Your feet move naturally, drawn by the gentle scent. A few steps later, you see a flower stall welcoming customers.)
Oh, so this is where it came from.
strings.(노점 수레 뒤에 앉아 있던 한 청년이 인기척을 느꼈는지 자리에서 일어난: (A young man sitting behind the stall's cart rises, apparently noticing your approach.)
Hello... I noticed a floral scent from somewhere and followed it here...
strings.멀리까지 꽃향기가 전해질 정도로 진했나요?: Was the fragrance strong enough to travel that far?
strings.진하다기 보다는 뭐라고 해야 하죠. 과일의 과즙같이 상큼한 향도 있었고,: Rather than strong... How should I put it? There was a fresh scent like fruit juice, and something that tickled my nose like a rich perfume...
There was also a scent like something I'd smelled by the sea.
strings.(무표정한 청년이 %s의 이야기를 듣더니 살짝 놀란다.): (The expressionless young man looks slightly surprised by %s's words.)
...You identified the scents of all three kinds of flowers I brought today. That's impressive.
Oh, did I? Maybe it's just because I like all flowers.
strings.(청년이 가볍게 웃으면서 자기소개를 한다.): (The young man smiles lightly and introduces himself.)
strings.저는 아드리안이라고 해요. 화원에서 직접 키운 꽃을 가져와 판매하고 있어: I'm Adrian. I bring flowers I've grown myself at my nursery and sell them here. But I don't think I've seen you in the plaza before...
That's right. This is my first visit to Glaston.
strings.실례가 되지 않으면 이름을 알려주실 수 있을까요?: If you don't mind, could you tell me your name?
strings.(아드리안은 내 소문을 듣지 못한 거 같네.): (It seems Adrian hasn't heard the rumors about me.)
You don't seem to be looking for flowers.
I'm sorry. I'm working on something and asking people a few questions...
It's all right. Please go ahead.
strings.이런 것도 괜찮을까요? 꽃을 사러 온 꼬마들이 하는 이야기를 들었는데,: Would something like this help? I overheard some children buying flowers. They said strange sounds have been coming from their neighborhood...
Yes... There is a street called LaChouette, which people in Glaston regard as the slums.
strings.중앙 광장이나 주택 지구 같은 구역에 비해 낮은 지대에 있어서 좀 어둡긴: It's a little gloomy because it lies lower than areas like the central plaza and the residential district. That doesn't mean the people there are gloomy, though.
strings.하여튼…, 밤이 되면 라슈에트 안쪽, 지금은 사용하지 않는 수로 방향 쪽: Anyway... At night, from deep inside LaChouette, toward a disused waterway, they hear this sound.
strings.나가고 싶어, 나가고 싶어…. 누군가 이런 소리를 내며 흐느끼는데, 가까: 'I want to get out, I want to get out...' Someone sobs those words, but when they go closer, they can't hear anything.
strings.호기심 많은 아이들 몇이 어른들 몰래 탐험한다고 수로를 들어가봤는데도 아: A few curious children sneaked into the waterway to explore without telling the adults, but they found nothing.
strings.(빈민가 라슈에트의 수로? 흐음….): (The waterway in the LaChouette slums? Hmm...)
strings.너무 심각하게 생각하지 마세요. 소문은 그저 소문에 그치는 경우가 많아서: Please don't take it too seriously. Rumors often turn out to be nothing more than rumors...
strings.(나가고 싶다는 말, 분명….): (Those words, 'I want to get out'... Surely...)
strings.혹시 탐정이나 해결사 같은 일을 하시는 건가요?: Are you a detective or a troubleshooter?
I'm sure it isn't the sort of bad thing you're imagining.
strings.아, 그런데 여기 있는 이 분홍색 꽃은 뭔가요? 이 꽃만 향을 못 느끼겠: Oh, what is this pink flower? It's the only one whose scent I can't detect.
It's called Romeria. It has almost no fragrance, so it's often used for decoration.
strings.저도 처음엔 신기하게 생각했는데, 꽃이 자란 환경을 생각하면 이해되기도: I found that strange at first too, but it makes sense when you think about the environment it grows in.
strings.겨울에 피어나는 꽃이 따뜻한 봄을 만나려면 추위에 버텨야 하죠. 아마 혹: A flower that blooms in winter must endure the cold to greet the warmth of spring. Sometimes I wonder if its fragrance fades away while it weathers that harsh winter...
Because it passes through winter to welcome spring, it symbolizes new encounters.
strings.저에 대한 좋은 기억이 있었으면 해서 처음 뵙는 분에겐 이 꽃을 드리곤: I often give one to people I meet for the first time, hoping they'll remember me fondly. Would... that be all right?
strings.(아드리안이 꽃을 받고 기뻐하는 %s의 모습을 보고 환하게 웃는다. 그러: (Adrian smiles brightly at %s's delight in receiving the flower. Then he spots someone passing by and calls out loudly.)
strings.아…, 가버렸네요. 못 들었나 봐요. 아까 제게 소문에 대해 물어보실 때: Oh... She's gone. She must not have heard me. When you asked about rumors, I thought Edel might be able to help.
strings.엄청 똑똑하고 아는 것도 많아서 종종 고민 상담도 해줘요. 가끔 보면 저: She's very bright and knows all sorts of things. Sometimes she even gives me advice. There are times she seems more grown-up than I am.
strings.마침 산책 중인 것 같은데, 한번 에델하고 이야기해 보시겠어요?: She seems to be out for a walk. Would you like to talk with her?
strings.아, 에델이 우리 아드리안 화원의 꽃을 좋아해요. 꽃수레에서 몇 송이 꺼: Oh, Edel loves the flowers from Adrian's Flower Garden. Could you take a few from the cart and give them to her? Don't feel you owe me anything.
Yes, of course. I have all the flowers I could need.
Thank you, Adrian. I'll go meet Edel. Now, which flowers would she like?
strings.(콧노래를 부르던 작은 소녀가 누군가 자신을 부르는 소리에 주위를 두리번: (A little girl who was humming looks around at the sound of someone calling her.)
strings.아니에요, 아드리안이 불렀어요. 에델 맞죠?: No, Adrian called you. You're Edel, right?
strings.(소녀가 모르는 사람이 이름을 말하자 의심스러운 눈빛을 보인다.): (The girl gives a suspicious look when a stranger says her name.)
strings.제게 질문하시는 분은 누구실까요? 꽃도 들고 오신 걸 보면 제게 고백이라: And who might you be? You've even brought flowers. Are you here to confess your love?
Confess my love? Oh, no, nothing like that.
strings.맞다. 제 소개부터 할게요. 그래야 에델이 의심을 풀겠죠?: Right. Let me introduce myself first. That should ease your suspicions, shouldn't it?
strings.(모험가가 이름을 밝히자 에델이 살짝 놀란다.): (Edel looks slightly surprised when the adventurer gives their name.)
strings.혹시 그 모험가님이신가요? 최근에 아이에 섬에 표류된 사람들을 구하셨다는: Are you that adventurer? The one who recently rescued the people stranded on Aie Island...?
Of course. Hardly anyone in Glaston doesn't know your name, %s. Except Mr. Adrian.
strings.역시, 아저씨는 꽃 말고는 전혀 관심이 없거든요. %s 님, 그 꽃 저: I thought so. He has no interest in anything but flowers. %s, those flowers are for me, aren't they?
strings.(에델이 %s에게서 꽃을 받아 들고는 환하게 웃는다.): (Edel accepts the flowers from %s and smiles brightly.)
strings.고맙습니다. 저는 에델이에요. 그 꽃 아시죠? 에델바이스…. 그 에델이: Thank you. I'm Edel. You know the flower edelweiss? That's the Edel in my name.
strings.아드리안 아저씨가 절 불렀다는 건 %s 님과 이야기 해보라는 거겠죠?: If Mr. Adrian called me, it must mean he wanted me to talk with you, %s.
strings.제가 꽃을 좋아하니까 아저씨가 가져다주라고 하셨겠죠? 후후. 그래서 %s: I love flowers, so he must have asked you to bring them to me. Hehe. So, %s, what would you like to talk about?
strings.(아, 이래서 어른 같은 아이라고 한 거구나.): (Oh, so this is why he said she seems grown-up.)
strings.혹시 요즘 글래스턴에서 이상한 소문 같은 거 들은 적 있어요?: Have you heard any strange rumors in Glaston lately?
strings.글쎄요…. %s 님, 잠시만요…. 저, 잠깐 앉아도 될까요?: Let's see... %s, give me a moment... May I sit down for a little while?
I'll be fine if I sit for a bit. I'm rather frail, so this happens sometimes.
strings.10년 전, 열병을 앓았던 적이 있는데, 그때 죽다 살아났대요. 솔직히: Ten years ago, I had a fever that nearly killed me, apparently. Honestly, I don't remember it well, but I held on, and I'm all right now.
I've recovered enough to take walks with Mendelsmann XIV.
strings.집에서 키우는, 몸집이 곰 같이 큰 검은 강아지예요. 진짜 곰은 아니지만: He's our black dog, as big as a bear. He isn't really a bear, though.
strings.할아버지의 할아버지, 할아버지의 할아버지…, 옛날 할아버지께서 기르시던: My grandfather's grandfather, and his grandfather's grandfather... One of my ancestors had a dog, and our family has kept raising its descendants.
strings.지금 우리 멘델스만이 14대 째에요. 요즘 멘델스만이 기분이 안 좋아 보: Our current Mendelsmann is the fourteenth generation. He seems unhappy lately.
strings.매일 물고 다니던 장난감을 어디에 잃어버린 건지 집에 들어가서 안 나오더: He must have lost the toy he carried around every day. He went into his doghouse and won't come out.
I bought him new toys, but he doesn't seem to like them. Aww...
Oh... So getting him a good toy would help move our conversation along.
strings.(%s의 반응에 에델이 환한 미소와 함께 고개를 끄덕인다.): (Edel nods at %s's response with a bright smile.)
strings.(뭔가 당한 기분이 드는데…. 흐음. 커다란 강아지가 가지고 놀만한 장난: (I feel like I've been played... Hmm. What would make a good toy for a huge dog?)
strings.(최근에 본 개는 리시테아의 문 안에 있던 헬파이어 정도인데…. 가서 근: (The only dog I've seen recently was Hellfire inside Lysithea's gate... I should go look around there for something.)
strings.(에델이 %s에게 받은 커다란 검은 뼈를 보고 고개를 갸웃거린다.): (Edel tilts her head at the enormous black bone she receives from %s.)
strings.엄청나게 크고 단단한 막대기네요. 이거 어디서 구하셨어요?: What an enormous, hard stick. Where did you find it?
strings.…예전에 방문했던 곳에 있던 마수, 아니 엄청 큰 개가 가지고 놀던 장난: ...It's a toy that a demonic beast... I mean, a really big dog played with somewhere I visited before. It looked abandoned, so I picked it up.
strings.이거면 멘델스만이 좋아할 것 같아요. 고맙습니다. 그래서 제가 애들에게서: I think Mendelsmann will love it. Thank you. In return, I've learned a few things from the children.
strings.소문의 중심에 계신 %s 님께서 바로 움직이시면 소란스러운 일이 일어날: If you, the person at the center of all the rumors, act openly, it could cause a stir, %s.
For example, among people who don't think very highly of you, %s...
strings.%s 님이 멘델스만 장난감을 구해주시는 동안, 어린이집에서 제가 돌봐주는: While you were getting Mendelsmann's toy, %s, I asked the children I look after at the daycare for help. They had some interesting stories.
strings.(아, 일부러 이렇게 했다는 건 생각도 못 했네….): (Oh, I never imagined she'd arranged this deliberately...)
strings.아차, %s 님께 여쭤보려고 했던 게 있었는데…. 혹시 테오도르 교수님,: Oh, there was something I wanted to ask you, %s... Do you know Professor Theodore? He's my teacher, and he often tells me about you, %s.
strings.당연히 테오 교수님 잘 알죠. 제가 많은 도움을 받았어요. 그런데, 무슨: Of course I know Professor Theo well. He's helped me a great deal. What has he been saying?
Even after he went to Esnil, he sends me things to study by letter.
strings.최근엔 모로스 전투에서 %s 님이 참여하셨다면서 프레이오스와 이스트랜드가: Recently, he said you took part in the Battle of Moros, %s, and sent me piles of material about Freios and Eastland. About sixty pages this time, I think...
strings.이제 아이들 이야기 들으실 거죠? 누구 이야기가 재미있을 것 같으세요?: Now you'd like to hear the children's stories, right? Whose sounds most interesting?
strings.(흠…. 어떤 이야기를 먼저 듣지?): (Hmm... Which story should I hear first?)
A loves playing with the younger children, so he takes a whole group of them all over the place.
strings.글래스턴이 엄청나게 크잖아요. 그런데 안 가본 곳이 없어요. 광장은 물론: Glaston is huge, isn't it? But there's nowhere he hasn't been. He runs around the plaza and even the administrative district.
strings.라슈에트 거리를 막 뛰어다니다가 정말 이상한 분위기의 골목에 갔는데, 수: He was running through LaChouette Street when he entered an alley with a very strange atmosphere. An older boy with animal ears, like a beastfolk, was lying there wearing only trousers.
strings.곧 죽어갈 것처럼 보여서 나중에 먹으려고 챙겨둔 빵을 주니까, 뒤에 있던: He looked as though he was about to die, so A gave him the bread he'd saved for later. Then something like a golem behind him came over and thanked him.
He asked where there were lots of clothes, then flew away riding the golem.
strings.(…이 이야기는 노네임 같은데…. 이게 사실이면 라슈에트 어딘가에 있었다: (...That sounds like No Name... If it's true, he was somewhere in LaChouette...)
B likes to go out into the yard alone and stare blankly at the sky.
She was out there again at nap time, so I asked what she was doing...
And she said she'd seen a flying dolphin.
I asked how she could see a dolphin when this wasn't the sea...
She said a pink dolphin greeted her and flew off toward LaChouette Street.
I asked whether the other children had seen it, but none of them knew anything.
strings.(하늘을 나는 분홍 돌고래는 뭘까?): (What could a flying pink dolphin be?)
strings.제 베스트 프렌드 C는 어릴 적부터 좀 이상했어요. 물론, 지금도 어리고: My best friend C has been a little strange since we were small. Though we're still small, and she's still strange.
strings.돌아가신 할머니가 글래스턴에서 알아주는 점술가셨는데, 할머니를 닮아서 타: Her late grandmother was a well-known fortune-teller in Glaston. C takes after her and is very good with tarot. I suppose you'd say she has a strong intuition...
strings.얼마 전에 광장에서 사람들 점을 봐주고 있는데, 갑자기 주위가 어두워졌대: A little while ago, she was telling fortunes in the plaza when everything around her suddenly went dark.
strings.뭐지, 뭐지 하고 주위를 둘러보다가 문득 머리 위에 뭔가 있는 것 같아: She looked around, wondering what was happening, then felt something above her head and looked up...
strings.글래스턴인데, 위에 또 글래스턴이라고요?: She was in Glaston, with another Glaston above her?
strings.제가 본 게 아니라서 정확하진 않아요. C는 하늘 위에 또 다른 세상이: I didn't see it myself, so I can't be certain. C said it felt as though there was another world in the sky.
strings.너무 놀라서 여기저기 뛰어다녔는데, 거기서 키가 사람 두 배 정도 되는: She was so startled that she ran all over the place. Then she saw a monster about twice as tall as a person.
strings.겁에 질려 움직이지도 못하고 그러는 애한테 그 괴물이 네가 날 깨운 거냐: She was too frightened to move. The monster asked if she was the one who had awakened it, and she desperately said no.
strings.그러니까 괴물이 그럼 가라, 이러면서 다가오는데, 무서워서 자신도 모르게: Then the monster said, 'Go, then,' and approached. She was so scared she closed her eyes without thinking.
strings.물이 흐르는 소리가 들려와서 눈을 떠보니 자기가 타로점을 보고 있던 광장: She heard running water and opened her eyes to find herself back in the plaza where she'd been reading tarot. I don't know how much of it is true.
strings.앞에 있던 사람들은 얘가 왜 무서워하는지, 왜 겁먹고 있는지 몰라서 부모: The people in front of her couldn't understand why she was so frightened, so they called her parents.
strings.C의 부모님은 평소에 할머니가 그런 걸 많이 봐서 C도 그런 것 같다고: C's parents said her grandmother often saw things like that, so C must take after her.
strings.그래서 C는 지금 집에서 쉬고 있어요. 건강한 애가 집에만 있는 걸 보면: So C is resting at home now. Seeing such a healthy girl stuck indoors reminds me of how I used to be. I feel sorry for her.
strings.(흐음, 그 아이는 대체 뭘 본 걸까?): (Hmm. What on earth did that child see?)
strings.4. 흑마법을 배우고 싶은 D군(13세): 4. Boy D, age 13, aspiring dark mage
Maybe it's puberty, but D has been lost in his own little world lately.
strings.말을 걸면 필멸자여, 하찮은 영혼을 품고서도 잘도 살아있구나. 내게 원하: When you speak to him, he says things like, 'Mortal, you have done well to survive with such a paltry soul. What do you seek of me?'
Then the other children get offended and scold him. He's softhearted, so he says sorry. But it doesn't last long before he starts again.
strings.메기도가 어쩌고, 판데모니움이 어쩌고, 검은 용이 어쩌고 하는데, 전혀: He goes on about Megiddo, Pandemonium, and a black dragon. I couldn't understand any of it, so I asked Professor Theodore, and he explained.
strings.(판데모니움은 알겠는데, 메기도가 뭐였더라…?): (I know Pandemonium, but what was Megiddo again...?)
Apparently Pandemonium is a major city in the Demon Realm, like Glaston...
strings.메기도는 현재의 마족들도 잘 모를 만큼 고대 시절에 존재했던 곳이 아닐까: He thought Megiddo might have existed so long ago that even today's demons know little about it.
strings.어쨌든 D군이 쓰는 그 말이 나쁜 말이니까 그런 말을 쓰지 못하게 하라고: Anyway, he said the things D was saying were bad and insisted I stop him using those words. I just finished scolding him again.
strings.D군은 그 이야기를 어디서 들었대요?: Where did D hear those things?
strings.언젠가 아이들끼리 마법청사에 견학갔다가 길을 잃었는데, 길을 찾아준 마법: Once, the children got lost on a field trip to the Magic Bureau. He overheard the mages who helped them find their way and thought it sounded cool, so he copied them.
strings.(마법사들이 뭘 하고 있기에 그런 이야기를 했던 걸까….): (What were those mages doing, to talk about things like that...?)
strings.이야기 들어주셔서 고맙습니다. 사실 어린 애들 이야기라고 잘 안 들어주실: Thank you for listening. Honestly, I thought you might not pay much attention to children's stories...
I'm the one who should thank you. It helped a lot.
strings.저는 이제 집에 가봐야 할 것 같아요. 아드리안 아저씨가 준 꽃은 병에다: I think I should go home now. I'll put Mr. Adrian's flowers in a pretty vase and make sure Mendelsmann gets his toy.
